theorems.name: Gaussian VaR Affine Invariance
theorems.description: For a gaussian loss L ~ N(μ, σ²), VaR_α(aL + b) = a·VaR_α(L) + b for a ≥ 0.

code.lean:
import MathFin.RiskMeasures.Gaussian

open MathFin

theorem gaussian_var_affine_thm (μ σ z a b : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ a) :
    MathFin.gaussianVaR (a * μ + b) (|a| * σ) z =
      a * MathFin.gaussianVaR μ σ z + b :=
  MathFin.gaussianVaR_affine μ σ z a b ha

theorems.name: Joint Standard-Deviation Triangle Inequality
theorems.description: √(σ₁² + 2·ρ·σ₁·σ₂ + σ₂²) ≤ σ₁ + σ₂ whenever σ₁, σ₂ ≥ 0 and ρ ≤ 1 — in particular for every correlation |ρ| ≤ 1. The substantive inequality behind gaussian subadditivity.

code.lean:
import MathFin.RiskMeasures.CoherentAxioms

open MathFin

theorem joint_stdev_triangle_thm {σ₁ σ₂ ρ : ℝ}
    (h₁ : 0 ≤ σ₁) (h₂ : 0 ≤ σ₂) (hρ : ρ ≤ 1) :
    Real.sqrt (σ₁ ^ 2 + 2 * ρ * σ₁ * σ₂ + σ₂ ^ 2) ≤ σ₁ + σ₂ :=
  MathFin.joint_stdev_le h₁ h₂ hρ

theorems.name: Gaussian CVaR: Rockafellar-Uryasev Variational Characterization
theorems.description: The Rockafellar–Uryasev variational theorem for the Gaussian loss L = μ + σ·Z with σ > 0, quantile-parametrized by z with Φ(z) = α < 1: CVaR_α = μ + σ·ϕ(z)/(1−α) is the least value of the objective c ↦ c + E[(L−c)⁺]/(1−α), and that least value is attained (IsLeast over the objective's range). The statement does not name the minimizer; the proof attains it at c = VaR_α (gaussianVaR).

code.lean:
import MathFin.RiskMeasures.RockafellarUryasev

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open MathFin

theorem gaussian_cvar_rockafellar_uryasev_thm (μ σ z α : ℝ) (hσ : 0 < σ)
    (hzα : MathFin.Phi z = α) (hα1 : α < 1) :
    IsLeast (Set.range (MathFin.ruObjective μ σ α)) (MathFin.gaussianCVaR μ σ z α) :=
  MathFin.gaussianCVaR_isLeast_ruObjective μ σ z α hσ hzα hα1

metadata.reference: Rockafellar-Uryasev 2000 (CVaR optimization)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full derivation (upgraded-properly 2026-06-04): the genuine Rockafellar-Uryasev VARIATIONAL theorem for the Gaussian loss L = mu + sigma*Z — IsLeast: CVaR_alpha is the least value of g(c) = c + E[(L-c)+]/(1-alpha) over all thresholds c, attained at c = VaR_alpha (gaussianCVaR_isLeast_ruObjective, RiskMeasures/RockafellarUryasev.lean). Minimality by the pointwise certificate (L-c)+ >= (L-c)*1_{Z>z} integrated against the Gaussian density; the attained value via the expected-shortfall closed form E[(Z-z)+] = phi(z) - z(1-Phi(z)) built on the truncated-first-moment primitive. Quantile-parametrized (z with Phi(z) = alpha; no Phi-inverse API exists at the Mathlib pin). Replaces the former algebraic additive-identity shadow. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Coherent Risk Representation (ADEH, finite state)
theorems.description: A coherent risk measure on a finite state space is the supremum of expected loss over a set of representing probability measures. The acceptance set is a closed convex cone, and a rejected position is separated from it by a representing density — the same Hahn–Banach separation the FTAP uses for the equivalent martingale measure. The risk-side face of the convex-duality unification.

code.lean:
import MathFin.RiskMeasures.AcceptanceSet

open scoped BigOperators

/-- **Coherent-risk representation (Artzner–Delbaen–Eber–Heath, finite state).** A coherent risk
    measure `ρ` on `ι → ℝ` is the least upper bound of expected loss `∑ qᵢ (-Xᵢ)` over its representing
    probability measures `q ∈ representingSet ρ`. The separating density realising the bound is the
    point-from-cone Hahn–Banach functional — the risk-side instance of the FTAP's separating root.
    Re-exports `MathFin.coherentRisk_isLUB`. -/
theorem coherent_risk_representation {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] {ρ : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ}
    (hρ : MathFin.IsCoherentRisk ρ) (X : ι → ℝ) :
    IsLUB ((fun q => ∑ i, q i * (- X i)) '' MathFin.representingSet ρ) (ρ X) :=
  MathFin.coherentRisk_isLUB hρ X

metadata.reference: Artzner–Delbaen–Eber–Heath 1999 (coherent measures of risk); finite-state representation via convex duality
metadata.formalization_scope: Full proof of the finite-state ADEH representation re-exported from MathFin/RiskMeasures/AcceptanceSet.lean: a coherent risk measure (the four ADEH axioms, bundled as IsCoherentRisk) equals the supremum (stated as IsLUB) of expected loss over its representing probability measures. Closedness of the acceptance set is derived from the axioms (ρ convex hence continuous on ℝ^ι), not assumed. The least-upper-bound direction separates the rejected position X + (ρX-ε)·1 from the acceptance cone via the point-from-cone primitive MathFin.exists_separating_of_not_mem_cone and normalises the separating functional to a representing density — the same Hahn–Banach root as the FTAP. No axioms beyond Mathlib defaults.

theorems.name: Worst-Case Loss as a Coherent-Risk Instance

Its coherence is a separate theorem (worstCase_isCoherent) and not part of this entry's statement.

A concrete, recognisable instance making the finite-state ADEH representation tangible. No axioms beyond Mathlib defaults.

theorems.name: von Neumann-Morgenstern Axioms for Expected Utility
theorems.description: Expected utility over finite-outcome lotteries is affine in the lottery mixture; the induced preference satisfies independence and Archimedean continuity (an indifference weight α ∈ (0,1) exists); and, for normalized lotteries, the preference is invariant under positive affine rescaling of the utility. Completeness and transitivity of the preference are proved in the source module (prefersEU_total, prefersEU_trans) but are not restated in this entry. Soundness direction only: the vNM representation theorem (axioms imply an expected-utility form) is not delivered.

code.lean:
import MathFin.RiskMeasures.VonNeumannMorgenstern

open MathFin

/-- The pivot of the vNM development: expected utility is affine in the lottery mixture,
    `EU(αp + (1−α)q) = α·EU(p) + (1−α)·EU(q)`. Needs no hypotheses on the lotteries —
    it is linearity of the finite sum, and it is exactly what fails for the non-linear
    functionals invented to explain the Allais paradox. -/
theorem vnm_expected_utility_mix
    {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (u : ι → ℝ) (α : ℝ) (p q : ι → ℝ) :
    MathFin.expectedUtility s u (MathFin.mix α p q)
      = α * MathFin.expectedUtility s u p + (1 - α) * MathFin.expectedUtility s u q :=
  MathFin.expectedUtility_mix s u α p q

/-- vNM independence: mixing a common lottery into both sides preserves the
    expected-utility preference, at any nonnegative weight. -/
theorem vnm_independence
    {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (u : ι → ℝ) {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 ≤ α)
    {p q r : ι → ℝ} (h : MathFin.prefersEU s u p q) :
    MathFin.prefersEU s u (MathFin.mix α p r) (MathFin.mix α q r) :=
  MathFin.prefersEU_independence s u hα h

/-- vNM continuity (the Archimedean axiom): strictly between a better and a worse lottery,
    some strict mixture of the outer pair is exactly indifferent to the middle one; the
    weight is exhibited as the position of the middle utility on the outer utility
    interval, not obtained from a limit. -/
theorem vnm_continuity
    {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (u : ι → ℝ) {p q r : ι → ℝ}
    (hpq : MathFin.expectedUtility s u q < MathFin.expectedUtility s u p)
    (hqr : MathFin.expectedUtility s u r < MathFin.expectedUtility s u q) :
    ∃ α : ℝ, 0 < α ∧ α < 1 ∧
      MathFin.expectedUtility s u (MathFin.mix α p r) = MathFin.expectedUtility s u q :=
  MathFin.prefersEU_continuity s u hpq hqr

/-- vNM cardinality: a positive affine rescaling of the utility induces exactly the same
    preference on lotteries — utility is cardinal only up to origin and scale. -/
theorem vnm_affine_invariance
    {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (u : ι → ℝ) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
    {p q : ι → ℝ} (hp : ∑ i ∈ s, p i = 1) (hq : ∑ i ∈ s, q i = 1) :
    MathFin.prefersEU s (fun i ↦ a * u i + b) p q ↔ MathFin.prefersEU s u p q :=
  MathFin.prefersEU_affine_invariant s u ha hp hq

theorems.name: Step-Spectrum Spectral Risk Measures Are Coherent Mixtures of Expected Shortfall
theorems.description: For weights w_k ≥ 0 with Σ w_k = 1 and levels α_k ∈ (0, 1), the spectral risk measure ρ_φ(X) = ∫₀¹ φ(u) VaR_u(X) du with the nondecreasing step spectrum φ = Σ_k w_k (1 − α_k)⁻¹ 1_(α_k, 1) equals Σ_k w_k ES_{α_k}(X) for every integrable loss X, and is a coherent risk measure on the integrable losses (monotone, translation invariant, positively homogeneous, subadditive). Acerbi's theorem for a general nondecreasing spectrum is not proved; only these step spectra are.

code.lean:
import MathFin.RiskMeasures.Spectral

open MeasureTheory Set
open MathFin

/-- The spectral risk of the step spectrum `∑ₖ wₖ (1 − αₖ)⁻¹ 𝟙_{(αₖ, 1)}` is the mixture
`∑ₖ wₖ ES_{αₖ}(X)` of expected shortfalls. -/
theorem spectral_step_spectrum_eq_es_mixture_thm {ι Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {X : Ω → ℝ} (hX : Integrable X P) (s : Finset ι)
    (w : ι → ℝ) {α : ι → ℝ} (hα : ∀ k ∈ s, α k ∈ Ioo 0 1) :
    spectralRiskMeasure (fun u ↦ ∑ k ∈ s, w k * esSpectrum (α k) u) X P =
      spectralRiskFinite s w fun k ↦ expectedShortfall X P (α k) :=
  spectralRiskMeasure_sum_esSpectrum hX s w hα

/-- For weights `w ≥ 0` summing to one, the step-spectrum spectral risk measure is a coherent
risk measure on the integrable losses. -/
theorem spectral_step_spectrum_coherent_thm {ι Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (s : Finset ι) {w α : ι → ℝ}
    (hw : ∀ k ∈ s, 0 ≤ w k) (hw1 : ∑ k ∈ s, w k = 1) (hα : ∀ k ∈ s, α k ∈ Ioo 0 1) :
    IsCoherentRiskMeasure P
      (spectralRiskMeasure (fun u ↦ ∑ k ∈ s, w k * esSpectrum (α k) u) · P) :=
  isCoherentRiskMeasure_spectralRiskMeasure_sum_esSpectrum s hw hw1 hα

theorems.name: Expectiles Are Elicited by the Asymmetric Squared Loss
theorems.description: For α ∈ (0, 1) and every probability law μ on ℝ with finite second moment, each expected asymmetric squared loss ∫ α((y − e)⁺)² + (1 − α)((e − y)⁺)² dμ(y) is finite, and the α-expectile of μ (the root e of α E[(Y − e)⁺] = (1 − α) E[(e − Y)⁺]) is its unique minimizer over forecasts e ∈ ℝ. Also, for an integrable Y the 1/2-expectile is the mean E[Y].

open MeasureTheory Set
open MathFin

/-- The asymmetric squared loss `α ((y − e)⁺)² + (1 − α) ((e − y)⁺)²` strictly elicits the
`α`-expectile on the probability laws on `ℝ` with finite second moment. -/
theorem expectile_elicitable_thm {α : ℝ} (hα : α ∈ Ioo 0 1) :
    StrictlyElicits (expectileLoss α) (fun μ ↦ expectile α id μ)
      {μ | IsProbabilityMeasure μ ∧ MemLp id 2 μ} :=
  strictlyElicits_expectileLoss hα

/-- The `1/2`-expectile of an integrable loss is its mean. -/
theorem expectile_half_thm {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {Y : Ω → ℝ} (hY : Integrable Y P) :
    expectile (1 / 2) Y P = ∫ ω, Y ω ∂P :=
  expectile_half hY

StrictlyElicits is the strict-consistency notion of MathFin/RiskMeasures/Elicitability.lean (finite expected scores, unique minimizer). theorems.name: Gaussian VaR and ES Are Standard-Deviation Premium Principles
theorems.description: For a loss X with law N(m, v) and α ∈ (0, 1): VaR_α(X) = E[X] + Φ⁻¹(α)·sd(X), the standard-deviation principle with loading Φ⁻¹(α); and if v ≠ 0, ES_α(X) = E[X] + (ϕ(Φ⁻¹(α))/(1 − α))·sd(X), the principle with loading ϕ(Φ⁻¹(α))/(1 − α), where ϕ is the standard normal density. VaR and ES are the library's general (quantile-based) definitions.

theorems.name: Expected-Utility Acceptance Sets Are Convex but Need Not Be Coherent
theorems.description: On a finite state space with weights p ≥ 0, a position X is acceptable to an expected-utility agent with utility u and wealth W if u(W) ≤ Σ p_i u(W + X_i). For concave u, every convex combination of two acceptable positions is acceptable. A binary Kelly bet of fraction f at odds b (win probability p) is acceptable under log utility at unit wealth iff its expected log-growth p log(1 + fb) + (1 − p) log(1 − f) is nonnegative. On a fair coin at unit wealth, log utility accepts X = (1/2, −1/4) but rejects 3X, so no coherent risk measure on positions (Artzner–Delbaen–Eber–Heath axioms) has the log-utility acceptance set {X : ρ(X) ≤ 0} (log is Mathlib's Real.log, equal to log|x| at nonpositive wealth). Only this explicit counterexample is proved, not a general statement about all strictly concave utilities.

code.lean:
import MathFin.RiskMeasures.UtilityDerivation

open MathFin

/-- A concave utility makes the acceptance set convex. -/
theorem utility_acceptance_convex_thm {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (p : ι → ℝ) (u : ℝ → ℝ)
    (W : ℝ) (hp : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ p i)
    (hu : ∀ x y : ℝ, ∀ α : ℝ, 0 ≤ α → α ≤ 1 →
      α * u x + (1 - α) * u y ≤ u (α * x + (1 - α) * y))
    {X Y : ι → ℝ} {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hα1 : α ≤ 1)
    (hX : acceptableUnderUtility s p u W X) (hY : acceptableUnderUtility s p u W Y) :
    acceptableUnderUtility s p u W (fun i ↦ α * X i + (1 - α) * Y i) :=
  acceptableUnderUtility_convex s p u W hp hu hα hα1 hX hY

/-- A Kelly bet is acceptable under log utility at unit wealth iff its expected log-growth is
nonnegative. -/
theorem kelly_log_acceptance_thm (p b f : ℝ) :
    acceptableUnderUtility Finset.univ ![p, 1 - p] Real.log 1 ![f * b, -f] ↔
      0 ≤ kellyGrowth p b f :=
  acceptableUnderUtility_log_iff_kellyGrowth p b f

/-- The log-utility acceptance set of a fair coin is the acceptance set of no coherent risk
measure: it is not a cone. -/
theorem log_acceptance_not_coherent_thm :
    ¬∃ ρ : (Fin 2 → ℝ) → ℝ, IsCoherentRisk ρ ∧
      ∀ X, ρ X ≤ 0 ↔ acceptableUnderUtility Finset.univ ![1 / 2, 1 / 2] Real.log 1 X :=
  not_exists_isCoherentRisk_log_acceptance

Schied, Convex Measures of Risk and Trading Constraints, Finance and Stochastics 6(4) (2002), 429–447; J. L. Kelly, A New Interpretation of Information Rate, Bell System Technical Journal 35(4) (1956), 917–926

theorems.name: Euler Allocation of Gaussian Portfolio VaR
theorems.description: For a Gaussian vector X of risk-factor changes, weights w with positive portfolio variance wᵀΣw (Σ the covariance kernel of X) and α ∈ (0, 1): the value-at-risk of the portfolio loss Σ wᵢXᵢ is its mean Σ wᵢ E Xᵢ plus the parametric VaR Φ⁻¹(α)√(wᵀΣw), and the component VaRs wᵢ Φ⁻¹(α)(Σw)ᵢ/√(wᵀΣw) sum to VaR_α(Σ wᵢXᵢ) − Σ wᵢ E Xᵢ. For any symmetric kernel with positive portfolio variance, the marginal VaRs α(Σx)ᵢ/√(xᵀΣx) are the partial derivatives of x ↦ α√(xᵀΣx): its derivative along any direction d is Σ dᵢ · marginalVaRᵢ.

import MathFin.RiskMeasures.ComponentVaR

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set
open MathFin

/-- The VaR of a Gaussian portfolio loss is its mean plus the parametric VaR at `Φ⁻¹(α)`. -/
theorem gaussian_var_eq_portfolioVaRN_thm {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {Ω : Type*}
    {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω} {X : ι → Ω → ℝ} {α : ℝ}
    (hX : HasGaussianLaw (fun ω ↦ (X · ω)) P) (w : ι → ℝ) (hα : α ∈ Ioo 0 1) :
    valueAtRisk (fun ω ↦ ∑ i, w i * X i ω) P α =
      ∑ i, w i * P[X i] +
        portfolioVaRN Finset.univ w (fun i j ↦ cov[X i, X j; P]) (PhiInv α) :=
  valueAtRisk_portfolio_gaussian_eq_portfolioVaRN hX w hα

theorem component_var_gaussian_euler_thm {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {Ω : Type*}
    {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω} {X : ι → Ω → ℝ} {α : ℝ}
    (hX : HasGaussianLaw (fun ω ↦ (X · ω)) P) (w : ι → ℝ) (hα : α ∈ Ioo 0 1)
    (hvar : 0 < portfolioVarN Finset.univ w fun i j ↦ cov[X i, X j; P]) :
    ∑ i, componentVaR Finset.univ w (fun i j ↦ cov[X i, X j; P]) (PhiInv α) i =
      valueAtRisk (fun ω ↦ ∑ i, w i * X i ω) P α - ∑ i, w i * P[X i] :=
  sum_componentVaR_eq_valueAtRisk_sub hX w hα hvar

theorems.name: SA-CCR Effective Notional as a Standard Deviation
theorems.description: Let D₀, D₁, D₂ be the signed effective notionals of the three maturity buckets of an SA-CCR interest-rate hedging set. If Z₀, Z₁, Z₂ are square-integrable random variables whose covariances equal the Basel CRE52.57 supervisory correlations (1 on the diagonal, 0.7 between adjacent buckets, 0.3 between the first and third), then the effective notional √(D₀² + D₁² + D₂² + 1.4D₀D₁ + 1.4D₁D₂ + 0.6D₀D₂) equals the standard deviation of Σ Dᵢ Zᵢ. Also, the radicand is nonnegative for every D. The factors Z are a hypothesis of the statement, not part of the Basel formula, and their existence is not constructed here.

code.lean:
import MathFin.RiskMeasures.SACCRExposure

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open MathFin

/-- Under unit-variance bucket factors with the supervisory correlations, the SA-CCR
interest-rate effective notional is the standard deviation of the hedging-set exposure. -/
theorem saccr_effnotional_std_dev_thm {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure Ω}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {Z : Fin 3 → Ω → ℝ} (hZ : ∀ i, MemLp (Z i) 2 μ)
    (hcov : ∀ i j, cov[Z i, Z j; μ] = saccrIRCorrelation i j) (D : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    effNotionalIR (D 0) (D 1) (D 2) = √Var[∑ i, D i • Z i; μ] :=
  effNotionalIR_eq_sqrt_variance hZ hcov D

/-- The supervisory correlation matrix is positive semidefinite: the effective-notional radicand
is nonnegative. -/
theorem saccr_effnotional_radicand_nonneg_thm (D₁ D₂ D₃ : ℝ) :
    0 ≤ D₁ ^ 2 + D₂ ^ 2 + D₃ ^ 2 + 7 / 5 * D₁ * D₂ + 7 / 5 * D₂ * D₃ + 3 / 5 * D₁ * D₃ :=
  effNotionalIR_radicand_nonneg D₁ D₂ D₃

metadata.reference: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, The Basel Framework, CRE52.57 (interest-rate effective notional); Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, The standardised approach for measuring counterparty credit risk exposures (BCBS 279), 2014
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.effNotionalIR_eq_sqrt_variance and MathFin.effNotionalIR_radicand_nonneg (MathFin/RiskMeasures/SACCRExposure.lean). The effective notional is the square root of the Markowitz quadratic form portfolioVarN under saccrIRCorrelation (effNotionalIR_eq_sqrt_portfolioVarN), and portfolioVarN_covariance_eq_variance (MathFin/Portfolio/CovariancePSD.lean) identifies that form with Var[Σ Dᵢ Zᵢ]. SCOPE: the bucket effective notionals Dᵢ (supervisory duration, delta, maturity factor) are inputs; the factor model Z is a hypothesis that interprets the formula and is not part of the regulation.

theorems.name: Gaussian VaR of an Uncorrelated Portfolio Through the Herfindahl Index
theorems.description: For a Gaussian vector X of pairwise uncorrelated risk factors with common variance v, weights w and α ∈ (0, 1), the value-at-risk of the portfolio loss Σ wᵢXᵢ is Σ wᵢ E Xᵢ + √(v · HHI(w)) · Φ⁻¹(α), where HHI(w) = Σ wᵢ² is the Herfindahl–Hirschman concentration index of the weights.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Bridges.ConcentrationVariance

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set
open MathFin

/-- The VaR of an uncorrelated Gaussian portfolio is its mean plus `√(v · HHI(w)) · Φ⁻¹(α)`. -/
theorem uncorrelated_gaussian_var_herfindahl_thm {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω} {X : ι → Ω → ℝ} {α v : ℝ}
    (hX : HasGaussianLaw (fun ω ↦ (X · ω)) P) (hvar : ∀ i, Var[X i; P] = v)
    (hcov : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → cov[X i, X j; P] = 0) (w : ι → ℝ) (hα : α ∈ Ioo 0 1) :
    valueAtRisk (fun ω ↦ ∑ i, w i * X i ω) P α =
      ∑ i, w i * P[X i] + √(v * herfindahl Finset.univ w) * PhiInv α :=
  valueAtRisk_portfolio_gaussian_uncorrelated hX hvar hcov w hα

metadata.reference: H. Markowitz, Portfolio Selection, Journal of Finance 7(1) (1952), 77–91; A. J. McNeil, R. Frey and P. Embrechts, Quantitative Risk Management, revised ed. (2015), Example 2.11
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.valueAtRisk_portfolio_gaussian_uncorrelated (MathFin/Bridges/ConcentrationVariance.lean): valueAtRisk_portfolio_gaussian (MathFin/Bridges/GaussianRiskMarkowitz.lean) with the variance identity portfolioVarN_diag_eq_herfindahl, the ρ = 0 case of portfolioVarN_equicorrelated_eq_herfindahl (MathFin/Bridges/EquicorrelationConcentration.lean). SCOPE: Gaussian factors, pairwise uncorrelated with a common variance; the equicorrelated case is in EquicorrelationConcentration for the variance only.
